title: Wire document upload runtime

context.summary: Connect POST /v1/documents to concrete local object storage, document repository and BullMQ processing job dispatch.
context.background: TASK-8 added the upload service and API route surface, while TASK-15 wired document read repositories. TASK-18 makes the API server runtime capable of accepting uploads and enqueueing the first scan job.

in: Build local-fs object storage from Mindory config in the API runtime.
Build BullMQ processing queue and ProcessingJobDispatcher from Redis config.
Build DbProcessingJobStore and inject it into DocumentUploadService.
Inject DocumentUploadService into document routes in the server runtime.
Close the queue and database pool on Fastify shutdown.
Keep worker processors and jobs HTTP API out of scope.
Update docs and validation scripts for upload runtime wiring.

acceptance_criteria: API runtime constructs LocalFsObjectStorage from MINDORY_STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH when local-fs is configured.
API runtime constructs BullMqProcessingJobQueue from Redis config.
API runtime constructs DbProcessingJobStore and ProcessingJobDispatcher.
POST /v1/documents has a DocumentUploadService in the server runtime and can create document records plus scan jobs when dependencies are live.
Queue and database resources are closed through the API app close hook.
S3/MinIO, worker processors, jobs API and vector search remain future tasks.
Docs and validation scripts describe the new upload runtime boundary.

manual_checks: Confirm upload runtime is only local-fs by default.
Confirm S3/MinIO and worker processing are still out of scope.
Confirm no jobs HTTP routes were added.

risks: Runtime upload behavior still requires live PostgreSQL and Redis, which are not exercised in this task.
Async scan jobs are enqueued but not processed until TASK-19 wires worker processors.
S3/MinIO deployments still need a later adapter task or must use local-fs for MVP.
definition_of_done: Task status is changed to accepted or done.
Branch can be merged into master without unrelated changes.
